hints.title: Time-Interval Weighted Unit Pricing
hints.text: Join sales to the corresponding price active during the purchase date interval, dividing total revenue by total units.

hints.title: Between Date Equi-Join with Fallback
hints.text: Left join prices with units sold where purchase date falls between start and end dates. Coalesce results to zero if no units were sold.

hints.title: Average Selling Price Blueprint
hints.text: select p.product_id, ifnull(round(sum(p.price * u.units) / sum(u.units), 2), 0) as average_price from Prices p left join UnitsSold u on p.product_id = u.product_id and u.purchase_date between p.start_date and p.end_date group by p.product_id.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT p.product_id,
       IFNULL(ROUND(SUM(p.price * u.units) / SUM(u.units), 2), 0) AS average_price
FROM Prices p
LEFT JOIN UnitsSold u
  ON p.product_id = u.product_id
 AND u.purchase_date BETWEEN p.start_date AND p.end_date
GROUP BY p.product_id;
```

complexity.notes: Interval join and grouped weighted sum executes linearly relative to input table sizes.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Inner joining drops products that have defined price intervals but recorded zero sales.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Interval predicate within join condition filters transactions without quadratic row scans.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of IFNULL / COALESCE to handle products with zero units sold and ROUND(..., 2).

SELECT p.product_id,
       COALESCE(ROUND(SUM(p.price * u.units)::numeric / NULLIF(SUM(u.units), 0), 2), 0) AS average_price
FROM Prices p
LEFT JOIN UnitsSold u
  ON p.product_id = u.product_id
 AND u.purchase_date BETWEEN p.start_date AND p.end_date
GROUP BY p.product_id;

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def average_selling_price(prices: pd.DataFrame, units_sold: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    merged = prices.merge(units_sold, on='product_id', how='left')
    valid = merged[(merged['purchase_date'].isnull()) | 
                   ((merged['purchase_date'] >= merged['start_date']) & (merged['purchase_date'] <= merged['end_date']))]
    valid['revenue'] = valid['price'] * valid['units']
    grouped = valid.groupby('product_id').agg(
        total_rev=('revenue', 'sum'),
        total_units=('units', 'sum')
    ).reset_index()
    grouped['average_price'] = (grouped['total_rev'] / grouped['total_units']).fillna(0).round(2)
    return grouped[['product_id', 'average_price']]
solutions.approach: Pandas Merge and Interval Mask with Zero Fill
